title: U5: Stage-decomposed benchmark harness
description:
Phase 1 — Measure. THIS UNIT IS THE GATE: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes. U30, U15, U16, U17, U18, U19, U20, U23, and U26 must pass its regression mode before landing. Its baseline must exist BEFORE any Phase 3/4 ranking-affecting change lands.

## Goal
One harness that measures retrieval quality and stage-level latency, and serves as the regression gate.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R27: stage-level timing decomposition — "query inference, generation lookup, filter construction, vector scan, top-K, metadata hydration, fusion, reranking, packing"; reports "Recall@10/50, MRR, nDCG@10, p50/p95 latency, decoded bytes per query, and index build time"; "fixture-judged relevance labels (shadow result disagreement is not a label)".
- R28: "Hardware-level bets (AoSoA layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades, GEMM micro-batching, mmap layouts) land only on measured wins against the row-major f32 exact baseline with stable tie-breaking, reporting recall and ranking quality for every approximate variant."
- KTD17: "nDCG@10 regression tolerance <= 2 percentage points versus the stored snapshot, averaged over 3 runs, with no single run below baseline - 5 points; Recall@50 uses the same 2/5-point tolerance pair; p95 latency tolerance is +10% versus snapshot. Store the tolerance values themselves as versioned config next to the snapshot so tightening them later is a reviewed change, not a silent drift."
- KTD22: labels resolve through the canonical relevance identity built in U4.
- KD6/Success Criteria: the U5 measurement RECORDS whether TS-only plus Phase 0/1 already met the latency and recall thresholds — an auditability record, not a stop condition.

## Key files
- packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-retrieval.ts (new), reusing patterns from packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-message-fts.ts; Rust side hooks later via U10's criterion benches.

## Approach
1. Metrics: Recall@10/50, MRR, nDCG@10, reranker lift, duplicate rate, context tokens per useful result, p50/p95 latency, decoded bytes per query, index build time.
2. Stage decomposition: a labeled timer around each pipeline seam, recording BOTH inclusive and exclusive span duration. Lexical and dense lanes run in parallel, so account for overlapping spans on the CRITICAL PATH, not by summing every stage's elapsed time — a naive sum over parallel spans would either exceed wall-clock time or misattribute a regression to the wrong stage.
3. Parameter matrix: corpus 1K-1M, dims 128-1024, K 5-100, filter selectivity 0.1%-100%, cold/warm page cache, concurrency 1-8; run on ARM NEON and x86 AVX2 hosts.
4. Baseline the current pipeline per-source and fused BEFORE any Phase 3/4 change lands; store results as versioned JSON snapshots for regression comparison. Record the TS-only-vs-thresholds measurement (KD6).
5. Acceptance policy per KTD17 (quoted above); tolerance values live as versioned config next to the snapshot.
6. Relevance labels resolve through KTD22's canonical relevance identity so a post-migration corpus (claims/revisions/retrieval-documents) scores correctly against legacy-vocabulary labels.

## Test scenarios
- Harness on the seeded synthetic corpus reproduces identical quality metrics across two runs (determinism).
- Inclusive stage-span durations sum to within tolerance of end-to-end time; EXCLUSIVE (critical-path) durations are used for regression attribution; a fixture with overlapping lexical/dense lanes does not fail the accounting check purely from parallelism.
- Regression mode exits nonzero when nDCG@10 or Recall@50 breaches the KTD17 2/5-point rule vs a stored snapshot, or p95 latency exceeds +10%; passes when within tolerance across 3 runs.
- A result whose storage identity changed across the claims migration (same canonical relevance identity, different underlying row shape) scores as present, not as a false recall loss.

## Verification
- Harness runs clean on the fixture corpus in CI-sized configuration; baseline snapshot and its versioned tolerance config committed together.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (harness + matrix + acceptance policy) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: full matrix runs on benchmark hosts only, CI runs the CI-sized config; perf: this unit IS the perf control plane; ponytail-review: critical-path span accounting is load-bearing for parallel lanes, keep; invariant-test-review: regression oracle is the exact KTD17 2/5pp + 10% rule with tolerances as versioned config - no silent drift; test-strategy: determinism examples + versioned snapshot comparison as the gate form

title: U30: Query-purpose default flip (benchmark-gated)
description:
Phase 1 — Measure. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; this is a ranking-affecting change and must pass U5 regression mode before landing (KTD20 makes the dependency explicit).

## Goal
unifiedSearch embeds queries as queries by default, landed against a measured baseline rather than ahead of it.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R24: "The query-vs-passage purpose is honored end to end: unifiedSearch defaults to query purpose, and the local provider applies purpose templates instead of ignoring the parameter." (The provider-side template work is U24; this unit flips the default.)
- R27: the judged benchmark gates ranking changes.
- KTD20: "U3's default embed-purpose change ships only after U5's benchmark can compare the pre-change (passage-default) and post-change (query-default) paths. A ranking-affecting change landing before the judged baseline exists would let a real regression become the new reference undetected."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/embedding.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts (+ co-located tests)

## Approach
1. Change unifiedSearch's default embed purpose to "query" (the embedText fallback currently embeds as passage); the shadow-measurement path uses "query" too so comparisons stay fair.
2. Run the U5 harness comparing the pre-change (passage-default) and post-change (query-default) paths on the judged corpus BEFORE merging; a regression beyond KTD17's tolerance blocks the change.

## Test scenarios
- unifiedSearch without an embedQuery override calls the provider with purpose "query" (spy on provider); existing callers passing wrappers keep their behavior.
- Shadow measurement records under the same purpose as primary.
- Benchmark comparison: the U5 harness run comparing passage-default against query-default purpose is committed alongside this unit's PR, showing no regression beyond KTD17's tolerance.

- KTD22: "Benchmark relevance labels use one canonical relevance identity independent of storage tables, with adapters mapping both legacy result IDs (memory:, chunk:, ...) and post-migration identities (claim, revision, retrieval-document) onto it before Recall/nDCG are computed. ## Approach
1. Export anonymized real queries from the existing measurement corpus (embedding_measurement_corpus), reusing its result-ID vocabulary (memory:, message:, chunk:, commit:, primer:, note:) as source labels.
2. Build judged fixtures across the audit's query categories: exact symbol/path, error message, architecture rationale, debugging history, user directive, current constraint, benchmark result, temporal, contradictory memory, paraphrased decision.
3. Labels are human/fixture judgments in versioned JSON; a small seeded synthetic corpus generator produces scale points (1K-1M documents) for latency runs where judged data is too small.
4. Canonical relevance identity per KTD22: define one relevance-ID scheme independent of storage tables, with an adapter mapping the legacy result-ID vocabulary onto it NOW (before U6-U8 exist) so labels never need retroactive rewriting once claims/retrieval documents replace memories rows.

- Anonymization: exported queries contain no raw user paths/secrets (redaction pass asserted against seeded sensitive fixtures).
- Synthetic generator is deterministic under a fixed seed (same corpus hash twice).
- Legacy-vocabulary adapter round-trips: a label written as memory:42 resolves to the same canonical relevance identity before and after a simulated claims migration of that row.

title: Retrieval and Storage Architecture Overhaul (U1-U30)
description:
# Retrieval and Storage Architecture Overhaul

Source plan: docs/plans/2026-08-16-001-refactor-retrieval-storage-overhaul-plan.md (authoritative: unit bodies U1-U30, Requirements R1-R33, KTD1-KTD30). Tasks under this epic are self-contained; the plan is the tie-breaker on conflict.

## Goal
Rebuild Magic Context's retrieval and storage architecture so semantic search stays fast and correct as history grows without bound: an immutable claims/evidence domain model, rebuildable search projections, an ID-first Rust dense engine (crates/mc-vector behind the ck-mc module), a cost-based query pipeline with global weighted RRF fusion, and convergence of write/index ownership on the existing module-authority machinery. Performance is a first-class design input throughout (KD2): quick wins land first, hardware bets are benchmark-gated.

## Success criteria
- Auto-search p95 <= 25 ms at a 100k-chunk / 384-dim scope on the benchmark hosts (ARM NEON and x86 AVX2), measured by the U5 harness.
- Active decoded index <= 128 MB at that scope ONLY IF a U15 compressed variant (int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix) wins its recall gate. The row-major f32 baseline reads ~154 MB at 100k x 384, so if no U15 variant passes, the memory threshold relaxes to ~154 MB, R12's ANN trigger fires, and the ANN decision in Scope Boundaries governs further scale.
- Fusion cutover (U18) shows recall/nDCG parity or better vs the pre-cutover baseline on the judged corpus, measured on the FINAL PACKED and deduplicated output (post-U19), not raw candidate lists.
- Steady-state persistence bytes per transform pass drop by an order of magnitude after the delta journal (U28), measured on the e2e Rust harness fixture.
- Zero dark-search windows: migration tests prove search returns results throughout the claims backfill and FTS tokenizer swaps.
- Search continues (degraded to lexical) with the daemon stopped, the index cold, or the embedding provider off.
- U5 records whether TS-only + Phase 0/1 already met the latency/recall thresholds before any Phase 3+ unit lands (KD6: auditability record, NOT a stop condition — the full Rust engine and authority convergence ship regardless).

## Stop conditions (every task inherits these)
Stop and surface instead of guessing when:
(a) evidence shows a session-settled decision cannot work (infeasible, destructive, wrong-thing);
(b) a schema migration would disable live processes outside the documented rollout order (R8: ship ALL binaries — OpenCode plugin, Pi plugin, CLI, ck-mc — with new version support first, THEN run the migration);
(c) a benchmark gate fails for a change the gate governs (R27, R28);
(d) work requires touching the prior audit's trust-boundary items (docs/fork-hardening-audit.md — out of scope).

## Phase map
- Phase 0 — Immediate wins (land before the architecture): U1, U2, U3
- Phase 1 — Measure (gates ALL ranking/model/layout/ANN changes): U4, U5, U30
- Phase 2 — Domain model and retrieval projection: U6, U7, U8, U9
- Phase 3 — Rust dense engine: U10, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15
- Phase 4 — Query pipeline and ranking: U16, U17, U18, U19, U20
- Phase 5 — Corpus enrichment: U22 lands BEFORE U21 (KTD28), then U21, U23
- Phase 6 — Embedding spaces and evaluation: U24, U25, U26
- Phase 7 — Storage and authority convergence: U27, U28, U29

Each unit lands green (bun test, cargo test --workspace, lint) before the next dependent unit starts. Each phase leaves the repo releasable: no half-applied migrations, no dark-search windows, abandoned experiment code removed. Benchmark-gated units (U30, U15, U16, U17, U18, U19, U20, U23, U26) must pass packages/plugin/scripts/benchmark-retrieval.ts regression mode vs the stored snapshot per KTD17 tolerances: nDCG@10 and Recall@50 each <= 2pp regression averaged over 3 runs with no single run below baseline-5pp; p95 latency +10%.

## Deferred / trigger-gated — NO tasks exist for these; do not build them (abstraction seams land in-plan)
- HNSW: add behind VectorIndex only when R12 thresholds cross (auto-search p95 > ~25 ms or active decoded index > ~128 MB per scope).
- IVF/PQ cold-history segments and the LSM-style hybrid index: only after corpus measurements justify; SQLite Vec1 stays shadow-evaluation only.
- Per-project search-projection sharding into separate index files: the projection/outbox design permits it; do not split until measurements justify.
- Postgres + pgvector server architecture: triggers are multiple hosts, hosted multi-user service, sustained concurrent writers, cross-device sync, per-tenant authorization.
- Learned rankers: only after relevance labels accumulate from the judged corpus.
- Outside the plan's identity: prior audit trust-boundary/fork-hardening findings; current-code-state retrieval; dedicated vector DB, ColBERT/multi-vector retrieval, embedding giant transcripts into single vectors.

## Definition of done (global)
All 30 units landed or explicitly re-scoped with the user; every fence-bumping migration shipped in R8 rollout order; success criteria recorded via the U5 harness on both reference hosts per KTD17's versioned acceptance policy; search works in every degraded mode (daemon off, rust mode off, embedding provider off, index cold, mid-backfill); no dead experiment code (U15 losers and the post-U18 legacy scoring path are REMOVED, not flag-parked, once their gates conclude); STRUCTURE.md updated for new modules/crates; docs/AUDIT-KNOWN-ISSUES.md / PARITY.md entries added where intentional divergences or accepted tradeoffs were created.

title: mc-host client: coalesced connect/route-open awaiters inherit the first caller's deadline

title: Smart-note evaluator: due-check backlog can starve compilation
description:
select_next_smart_note_evaluation (crates/mc-module/src/smart_note_evaluation.rs) applies strict phase priority (due > compile > liveness > fallback) per claim acquisition. A project with >= MAX_CLAIMS_PER_DRAIN (25) recurring due checks per timer tick consumes every drain iteration with 'due' claims, so notes needing compilation are never selected and stay uncompiled indefinitely despite a healthy evaluator. Raised by codex review on PR #12 (comment 3815004109).

Fix needs a fairness-policy design decision, not a mechanical patch: the selection function is a stateless pure function per acquisition (no drain-scoped state on the Rust side), and its semantics are pinned by the frozen characterization fixture smart-note-evaluation-golden.json (regeneration diff = semantic change requiring review, per PARITY.md). Candidate shapes: (a) per-phase quotas tracked drain-side via a phase hint in the claim request, (b) aging promotion using a 'needs compile since' timestamp (new snapshot/store field), (c) deterministic interleave. Whichever is chosen must update the golden/normative fixtures and PARITY.md.

The worker's per-drain dedup + break bounds the billable loop but cannot reach note 2 (releasing the claim just hands note 1 back). title: Fence module evaluator claim selection by checkout root
description: PR #12 review follow-up (codex 3814664230, claude 3814681244, claude 3814682201): two checkouts/worktrees sharing a root-commit project identity draw from one project-wide pending set, while each worker's filesystem capabilities bind to its own checkout root — so a file-dependent note can be compiled/evaluated against the wrong checkout. Three surfaces share the gap: (1) claim selection carries no originating route root; (2) the dream-timer drain falls back to any same-identity bridge when the exact (identity, root) bridge is missing (deliberate: an undrained module queue is worse, but it widens the wrong-root window); (3) the noteEvaluationAvailable write gate is identity-scoped, consistent with the current model but should tighten to exact-root once claims are fenced. This matches legacy sweep semantics (each registration's sweep evaluated the shared identity-scoped note set against its own root). A real fix persists the originating route root per note (or per claim) and fences claim selection to the worker's route — a store schema + protocol change, out of scope for PR #12.

title: Replace notes_fts trigram projection with bigram top-K dominance-walk engine (19x, search-lab validated)
description:
Replace the `notes_fts` trigram-FTS5 candidate projection with the bigram + top-K dominance-walk engine validated in the search-lab worktree (branch `search-lab`, `experiments/search-lab/`). Measured against a mirror of the production contract on a 12k-doc corpus: recall\@10 held at 100% of the production scorer's golden results, p95 candidate+rank latency 7.56ms -> 0.38ms (~19x), index bytes 35.3MB -> 16.4MB (2.2x). Full evidence: `experiments/search-lab/FINDINGS.md` on that branch; iteration ledger in the worktree's `autoresearch-results.tsv` (5 keeps / 12 discards, every alternative measured and falsified — hybrid trigram postings, dense-gram pruning, Roaring bitmaps, suffix array, galloping intersection all lost).

## Why this wins

The production scorer (`rankNotesForNeedle`, search.ts) computes `score = 2*exact + m/n + 0.5*(m=n>1)` with id-ascending tie-break — discrete and monotone in `(exact, m)`. The winning engine (`experiments/search-lab/engines/topk-walk.ts`) exploits this:

1. Bigram postings (sorted Uint16Array doc ids) generate exact-substring candidate supersets by rare-first intersection of at most 4 rarest grams; bigrams natively serve the 2-char needles that currently force `noteFtsQueryForNeedle` to return null and trigger a full `scopedNoteScan`.
2. Exact-token postings answer coverage (`m`) via binary search.
3. Candidates are walked in score-bucket dominance order (exact ∧ m=n first, token-only m=1 last), pulling ids ascending with early exit at K — the engine returns exactly K provable-top-K ids instead of feeding thousands of candidates to the scorer. Single-token needles: first K ids of the token posting, O(K), zero verification.
4. Lazy substring verification (`.includes` on prelowered text) only until K results exist. Keep native `.includes` — a JS fold-scan measured 5x slower; the prelowered store earns its bytes.
5. WORK_BUDGET fallback to plain superset union keeps pathological needles correct.

## Scope

- Add the posting index as a derived in-memory structure over searchable notes, built from SQLite (system of record — unchanged) on first search / startup, updated or invalidated on note write. Note cardinality is thousands: full rebuild is milliseconds-scale; do not build snapshot persistence.
- Replace `loadNoteSearchCorpus`'s FTS candidate path (`selectNoteCandidateIds` + `noteFtsQueryForNeedle`) with the engine; keep `scopedNoteScan` as the fallback for engine-unrepresentable needles (len<2) and error paths (matches the engine's own contract).
- `rankNotesForNeedle` stays the ranking authority. CRITICAL COUPLING: the engine's bucket order reproduces the scorer's dominance structure — if scoring changes, the walk must change with it. Port the lab's golden-set recall test (engine top-K vs full-scan scorer top-K on a seeded corpus, must be 100%) as the regression guard; add a property-style test comparing engine output to `scopedNoteScan`+`rankNotesForNeedle` over randomized needles.
- Retire `notes_fts` + `notes_search_view` (migrations.ts:239-251, migration 2900) only after the engine path is proven — follow the repo's FTS retirement discipline (see KTD29 note on 3q5.18: legacy query paths may need to outlive their replacement's flag).
- Coordinate with 3q5.18 (U17 dual lexical indexes): that unit rebuilds the retrieval_documents lexical lanes; this task owns only the notes candidate projection. The identifier-lane design there cites trigram — the lab evidence (bigram + dominance walk >> trigram FTS) should inform U17's identifier index choice.

## Non-goals

- No new dependencies, no LMDB/RocksDB (measured unnecessary at this cardinality; see FINDINGS.md "embedded DB" section).
- No change to message FTS (`message_history_fts`), RRF fusion, probe weighting, or the workspaced search union.

## Acceptance

- Golden-set recall test: engine candidates reproduce production top-K at 100% on the seeded corpus.
- Randomized equivalence test vs scoped-scan path passes.
- Existing search tests (search.test.ts, 3988-test plugin suite) green with zero behavioral diffs.
- Measured candidate-path latency improvement on a representative corpus recorded in the PR description (lab predicts ~19x at 12k docs).
- 2-char needle path no longer full-scans (test exists today at search.test.ts:2159 asserting the fallback — it must be updated to assert indexed behavior).
notes: RETIREMENT GATE (KTD29, per review): notes_fts + notes_search_view retire only after magic-context-3q5.19's RRF-cutover flag itself retires — not merely after the bigram engine path is proven. 3q5.19's flag-off path promises byte-identical legacy ranking across all sources, which needs the pre-cutover notes lexical surface intact. Implementation of the engine may proceed independently; only the drop step is gated.

title: U20: Reranker cascade (explicit search)
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (U5 gate reaches this unit through its U18 dependency): feature-flagged, DEFAULT OFF; the flag stays off unless the U5 benchmark shows positive reranker lift at acceptable p95. Explicit search only — auto-search NEVER invokes the reranker.

## Goal
Optional quality lift where latency is tolerable.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded work.
- R15 boundary (fusion stays the ranking scheme; reranking is a cascade on top for explicit search).
- KTD15: "Reranking is a cascade, explicit search only: cheap contiguous SoA feature model over all candidates -> cross-encoder only for the uncertainty set where score intervals overlap -> token-length batching and a hard deadline. Auto-search never pays reranker latency; it uses exact lookup + FTS + dense + fusion + a conservative confidence gate."
- KTD23: "...a maximum reranker pair/token count (enforced in U20 before cross-encoder dispatch). A deadline alone does not bound planner or reranker work started before it expires."

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/rerank.ts (+ test)
- packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-search/tools.ts
- config schema

## Approach
Feature-flagged, default off until benchmarked.
Stage 1: contiguous SoA feature model (lexical rank, dense rank, exact-match, source type, verification authority, trust, scope, recency, conflict state, supporting-source count, duplicate flag) over all candidates.
Stage 2: cross-encoder only on the uncertainty set (overlapping score intervals), token-length batched, hard deadline, PLUS an explicit maximum pair count and maximum total token count enforced BEFORE dispatch (KTD23) — a wide uncertainty set is capped, not just deadline-bounded, since a deadline alone does not stop unbounded encoding work already queued.

## Test scenarios
- Deadline expiry mid-stage-2 returns the stage-1 ordering (never blocks the tool call).
- Uncertainty-set selection: clearly separated candidates skip stage 2 (encoder spy shows zero calls); overlapping intervals trigger it.
- An uncertainty set wider than the pair/token cap is truncated to the cap BEFORE any cross-encoder call — the encoder never receives more pairs or tokens than the cap allows, independent of the deadline.
- Flag off -> pipeline output IDENTICAL to U18/U19.
- Feature extraction handles missing lanes (dense-off search) without NaN features.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark reports reranker lift; the flag stays off unless lift is positive at acceptable p95.
notes: judge-ruling: U5 gate reaches this unit transitively via U18 - direct edge intentionally omitted per adjudication (minimal graph, gate obligation carried in description); reduce-complexity: two-stage cascade is KTD15-mandated; less-code: default-off flag, no adoption until measured lift - trigger-gated by design, not speculation; perf: pair/token caps enforced BEFORE dispatch (KTD23) so a deadline is not the only bound; ponytail-review: auto-search never invokes it - latency budget protected; invariant-test-review: cap enforcement proven independent of deadline via encoder spy, NaN-free features on missing lanes, flag-off output identity; test-strategy: spy-based examples + flag-off identity golden

title: U19: Dedup + token-budget packing

## Goal
Delivered context maximizes usefulness per token.

## Governing constraints (quoted)

- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- packages/plugin/src/tools/ctx-search/tools.ts

## Approach
1. Collapse exact normalized hashes; SimHash/MinHash near-duplicate clusters with provenance preserved as cluster metadata; merge overlapping session ordinal intervals.
2. Greedy/CELF selection under the token budget; coverage of query atoms/claims/episodes/artifacts as bitsets so marginal gain is AND-NOT + POPCNT-style cheap.

## Test scenarios

- Overlapping compartment/message intervals merge; non-overlapping stay distinct.

title: U17: Dual lexical indexes (parallel-build swap)
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED (via U16's U5 dependency): U5 gates ranking changes; lexical-category metrics must be >= baseline.

RETIREMENT ORDER (KTD29 — note carried on both U17 and U18): "U17's old lexical tables and query paths stay live until U18's RRF-cutover flag itself is retired, not until U17's own backfill completes. U18's flag-off test promises byte-identical legacy ranking; that promise needs the pre-cutover lexical surface intact, so U17 cannot drop storage-memory-fts.ts's query paths on its own schedule."

## Goal
Prose and identifier lexical lanes replace Porter-everything.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R18: "Lexical retrieval has two representations over the retrieval projection: a prose FTS index without unconditional Porter stemming with per-column BM25 weights, and an identifier/path index (trigram or custom token characters) plus exact lookup tables; natural-language queries are never strict all-token conjunctions."
- R8: migration discipline (zero dark-search windows).
- KTD5: "FTS tokenizer changes are parallel-build swaps. Build the new-tokenizer table alongside (*_fts_v2 naming), backfill, swap atomically, drop the old table; a migration test asserts search returns results throughout. Tokenizers cannot be ALTERed on FTS5 tables." (Old-table drop applies to the swapped table; the legacy QUERY PATHS survive until U18's flag retires per KTD29.)
- KTD24: "The U17 FTS parallel-build swap uses a high-water-mark catch-up, not a point-in-time backfill snapshot. The backfill records the last-applied outbox position; once the initial backfill completes, a final catch-up pass replays every mutation after that position before the atomic rename — closing the gap where a write lands in the old table during a long backfill and never reaches the new one."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/lexical-index.ts (+ test)
- memory/storage-memory-fts.ts query paths STAY LIVE per KTD29 (retired with U18's flag, not by this unit)

## Approach
1. Prose FTS over retrieval_documents with unicode61 (no Porter) and per-column BM25 weights (title/claim 5-10x, rationale 2-3x, body 1x).
2. Identifier index: trigram FTS table (case-preserving) plus exact lookup tables for paths/SHAs/IDs/symbols extracted by the projection writer.
3. Parallel-build swap per KTD5 for any table replacing an existing FTS surface; multiple candidate lists per query (exact phrase, identifier, high-signal conjunction, broader disjunction, prefix/NEAR) generated from the U16 AST — never one all-token conjunction.
4. High-water-mark catch-up per KTD24 (quoted above).

## Test scenarios
- Migration test proves CONTINUOUS search: results present before, during (old table still serving), and after the swap on a seeded corpus (zero dark-search windows).
- Concurrent-write coverage: mutations applied to the old table during the backfill window are ALL present in the new table after the swap (the KTD24 catch-up closes the gap a point-in-time backfill would miss).
- Identifier recall: foo::bar and a path substring match via trigram where Porter-tokenized FTS missed them (regression pair fixture).
- Multilingual prose (non-English fixture) matches under unicode61 where the Porter-stemmed index failed.
- BM25 column weighting: a title hit outranks a body-only hit for the same term.
- Broad disjunction list recalls a document the strict conjunction missed; fusion (U18) ranks it sanely.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark lexical-category metrics >= baseline.
notes:
judge-ruling: U5 gate reaches this unit transitively via U16 - direct edge intentionally omitted per adjudication (minimal graph, gate obligation carried in description); KTD29: legacy lexical query paths retire ONLY when the U18 flag retires, noted here and on U18; reduce-complexity: dual index is R18-mandated; less-code: swapped old TABLE drops, but legacy QUERY PATHS stay until U18 flag retirement - deletion scheduled there; perf: per-column BM25 weights + trigram identifier lane; ponytail-review: candidate-list variety comes from the U16 AST, no second parser; invariant-test-review: continuous-search oracle (before/during/after swap) + concurrent-write catch-up coverage proves KTD24, paired Porter-vs-trigram regression fixtures discriminate; test-strategy: migration continuity test + paired regression fixtures
search-lab evidence (branch search-lab, experiments/search-lab/FINDINGS.md): for the notes candidate projection, bigram postings + top-K dominance walk beat trigram FTS5 19x at 100% recall; suffix array, Roaring bitmaps, and hybrid trigram postings all measured worse. Consider this when choosing U17's identifier-lane index (R18 says 'trigram or custom token characters' — bigram+walk is the measured winner for substring candidate generation). title: U18: Global weighted RRF cutover + progressive deepening
description:
Phase 4. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates ranking changes. THE CUTOVER'S GATE: fused metrics >= baseline on the judged corpus, measured on the FINAL PACKED and deduplicated output (post-U19), not raw candidate lists (Success Criteria: a benchmark pass on candidates that U19's packing then discards would not reflect what auto-search actually delivers).

FLAG LIFECYCLE (KTD29 — note carried on both U17 and U18): while this unit's cutover flag exists, U17's pre-cutover lexical tables and query paths stay live for the flag-off path. When the flag retires, the legacy scoring path is REMOVED (not flag-parked, per Definition of Done) and U17's old query paths retire with it.

## Goal
One coherent ranking scheme across all sources.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R15: "Cross-source ranking uses global weighted reciprocal-rank fusion; cosine, BM25, and synthetic scores are never mixed arithmetically, and the static source boosts (memory 1.3 / message 1.15 / commit 1.2 / primer 1.25) are removed."
- R16: "Trust and contradiction rules are hard filters, never soft relevance features; a highly similar contradicted claim is excluded, not down-ranked."
- R19: "RRF lanes deepen progressively: start with small per-lane candidate sets and stop when the maximum possible RRF contribution of unseen documents cannot overtake the current k-th result."
- KTD6: "RRF cutover is all-or-nothing per search call behind a single flag ... New sources (tool events) ship only under the new fusion."
- KTD18: "RRF lane weights start at 1.0 (uniform) across all lanes and are tuned only through the U5 benchmark, never by ad hoc per-source multipliers ... one versioned lane-weight table, checked in next to the benchmark snapshots, changed only when a benchmark run shows a specific lane's weight change improves nDCG@10 without regressing another lane."
- KTD19: "Trust and conflict filtering runs during lane construction, before ranks feed RRF — never after fusion ... The corrected order is LEX/DENSE lanes -> TRUST (per-lane eligibility) -> FUSE -> HYD." (This corrects the plan's earlier FUSE -> TRUST diagram ordering — an excluded contradicted candidate must not occupy a rank slot that shapes surviving documents' RRF scores.)

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts (+ test)
- config flag in packages/plugin/src/config/schema/magic-context.ts

## Approach
1. Replace 0.7 x cosine + 0.3 x reciprocal-rank, the single-source penalty, and the static source boosts with score(d) = sum over lanes of w_i / (k + rank_i(d)), k = 60 (consistent with the existing message/compartment RRF); w_i starts uniform 1.0 per KTD18.
2. Trust/conflict eligibility runs PER LANE before rank positions feed the fusion sum (KTD19) — an excluded candidate can never shape a surviving document's score.
3. Progressive deepening operates over eligible (post-trust-filter) ranks only: start 8-16 candidates per lane; stop when the max possible contribution of unseen eligible documents (sum of w_i/(k + next_rank_i)) cannot overtake the current k-th; deepen only unresolved lanes.
4. All-or-nothing flag per KTD6; auto-search additionally applies a conservative confidence gate before emitting a hint. The flag-off path uses U17's still-live pre-cutover lexical surface.

## Test scenarios
- Cross-source fixture: a document ranked #1 in two lanes outranks a single-lane #1 regardless of raw score magnitudes; no score-scale coupling (change one lane's raw scores, ranks unchanged).
- Deepening stop rule discriminated in BOTH directions: fixture where lane 2's unseen eligible max cannot overtake — assert lane 2 is NOT deepened; opposite fixture deepens it and changes the result.
- A contradicted claim with the highest cosine similarity never ENTERS a lane's eligible rank list, so it cannot affect fusion scores or appear in results (stronger than "absent from output" — proves the KTD19 ordering).
- Refill correctness: a candidate excluded by trust filtering after the initial 8-16 window is fetched does not silently shrink the returned count below the requested K — the eligible pool backfills before the stop rule locks in.
- Flag off -> BYTE-IDENTICAL legacy ranking, using U17's still-live pre-cutover lexical surface (guards the cutover).
- Auto-search gate: weak fused confidence emits no hint.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark fused metrics >= baseline on the judged corpus, measured on final packed/deduplicated output (post-U19).
notes: KTD29: while the cutover flag exists, U17 pre-cutover lexical surface stays live for flag-off; at flag retirement the legacy scoring path is REMOVED, not parked; reduce-complexity: one flag + one formula replaces three scoring mechanisms; less-code: net deletion at flag retirement; perf: progressive deepening bounds lane work (R19); ponytail-review: uniform w_i=1.0 start tuned only via benchmark (KTD18) - no hand-tuned boosts return; invariant-test-review: KTD19 ordering proven by never-enters-eligible-list oracle (stronger than absent-from-output), deepening rule discriminated in BOTH directions, refill correctness, flag-off byte-identity; test-strategy: constructed discriminating fixtures + byte-identical golden for flag-off

title: U16: Query analyzer + planner + index-time DF
description:
Phase 4 — Query pipeline and ranking. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; verification requires no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.

## Goal
One lexer + AST drives every lane; plans avoid work.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R17: "A deterministic query analyzer lexes queries into typed atoms (memory ID, commit SHA, file path, symbol, error code, quoted phrase, prose) and selects a plan per query; exact identifiers resolve via indexed lookup without embedding, and dense retrieval is skipped or deferred when lexical confidence is strong."
- KTD8: "The query analyzer is one maximal-munch lexer producing typed atoms and a query AST reused everywhere — exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion weighting, packing coverage. Document frequencies are maintained at index time (exact hashed counts for important atoms; a Count-Min Sketch is acceptable where overestimation only downweights a probe) — no query-time posting-count queries. Extends packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation."
- KTD23: the query-atom cap (landed in U3) is enforced in THIS lexer before planning.

## Key files
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/query-analyzer.ts (+ test), absorbing/extending literal-probes.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- DF bookkeeping in the projection writer (retrieval-projection.ts)

## Approach
1. Maximal-munch lexer -> typed atoms (memory ID, SHA, file path, symbol including camelCase/underscore/namespaced forms, error code, quoted phrase, temporal term, prose word); the AST is reused for exact lookup, FTS query formation, dense gating, highlighting, fusion, packing coverage.
2. Plan selection: exact IDs -> indexed lookup, no embedding; rare atoms with strong margin -> FTS first, dense skipped/deferred; mixed -> lexical first, dense conditional; prose -> parallel lanes. Dense embedding no longer starts unconditionally.
3. DF maintained at index time (exact for important atoms, CMS acceptable); no query-time posting counts.

## Test scenarios
- Lexer goldens: scaleConvolveVSym3, foo::bar, CR-297402306, packages/plugin/src/search.ts, HTTP_503, quoted phrases, mixed prose+identifier queries — each yields the expected atom types; identifiers are NOT split at underscores/dots.
- Memory-ID query plan performs ZERO embedding calls (provider spy).
- Rare-atom query with strong lexical margin skips the dense lane; an ambiguous query runs both.
- DF counts update on document add/remove; CMS overestimation only ever DOWNWEIGHTS a probe (property assertion on probe weighting).
- Empty and whitespace-only queries return empty plans without lane execution.

## Verification
- bun test; U5 benchmark shows no quality regression vs baseline on the judged corpus for lexical-heavy categories.
notes: reduce-complexity: one lexer reused by every lane REPLACES parallel probe logic - net complexity reduction; less-code: extends literal-probes.ts rather than a parallel implementation (KTD8); perf: index-time DF kills query-time posting scans, plans avoid work (dense no longer unconditional); ponytail-review: CMS only where overestimation is safe - already scoped; invariant-test-review: CMS safety proven as a property (overestimation only downweights), zero-embedding plan proven via provider spy; test-strategy: golden lexer examples + property for CMS + spy-based plan assertions

title: U15: Benchmark-gated layout/cascade/batching variants
description:
Phase 3. BENCHMARK-GATED: U5 gates all ranking/model/layout/ANN changes; every variant here lands ONLY on a measured win vs the U10 baseline (R28). Success-criteria coupling: the 128 MB decoded-index target is CONTINGENT on a U15 compressed variant winning its recall gate; if none passes, the memory threshold relaxes to the f32 baseline (~154 MB) and R12's ANN trigger fires (ANN itself stays deferred/trigger-gated — no HNSW work here).

## Goal
Measure the hardware bets; adopt only winners.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: "Hardware-level bets (AoSoA layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades, GEMM micro-batching, mmap layouts) land only on measured wins against the row-major f32 exact baseline with stable tie-breaking, reporting recall and ranking quality for every approximate variant."
- KTD10: "AoSoA block-transposed layout, int8/f16/Matryoshka-prefix cascades (conservative Cauchy-Schwarz pruning: skip when prefix_dot + query_tail_norm x candidate_tail_norm < kth_score, tail norms stored per candidate), and GEMM-style micro-batching of concurrent queries are benchmark-gated variants behind the same trait."
- Plan risk note (small-K reality check): "Top-K specialization and micro-batching pay off only under load; U12/U15 measure before adopting."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (variant modules + benches)

## Approach
Implement behind the VectorIndex trait and bench against the row-major exact baseline across the U5 matrix:
(a) AoSoA block-transposed layout;
(b) int8/f16 and Matryoshka-prefix cascade with tail-norm Cauchy-Schwarz pruning and oversampled full-f32 rerank;
(c) GEMM-style micro-batching for concurrent same-generation queries with a scheduler choosing shard-one-query / independent / batch (no added latency for isolated interactive queries).
Adopt per measured win; document losers and REMOVE their code (dead variants do not ship).

## Test scenarios
- Cascade preserves EXACT top-K on the comparator corpus when exact-mode pruning is enabled (tolerance-aware float handling asserted).
- Quantized recall reported per configuration; any recall < 1.0 variant is marked approximate and EXCLUDED from exact mode.
- Batching: 4 concurrent queries on one generation read vector pages once (bytes-touched counter) and match serial results.

## Verification
- Bench report vs the U10 baseline committed; only winning variants remain enabled.
notes: reduce-complexity: three bets behind the existing trait, no new seams; less-code: losers deleted, not flag-parked (plan-mandated); perf: this unit IS the measured-perf discipline (R28); ponytail-review: micro-batching pays only under load - measured before adopting per plan risk note; invariant-test-review: exact-mode cascade oracle = exact top-K preservation with tolerance-aware float compare, approximate variants must report recall and are excluded from exact mode; test-strategy: comparator property + bytes-touched counters + bench-gated adoption

title: U13: Module routes + TS client + queues/cancellation
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
The engine is reachable from both harnesses with deadlines, priorities, a transparent fallback, and a caller-authorization boundary that cannot be bypassed by a mis-scoped filter or a coalesced request.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R11: bounded, cancellable, priority-aware; "interactive queries have reserved capacity that backfills and background work cannot consume."
- R13: "Search stays functional when the Rust engine is unavailable (daemon down, rust mode off, index cold): the TypeScript scan path remains a working fallback, and cold-start windows degrade transparently."
- R32: "The dense search route derives a caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and never trusts a caller-supplied filter as authorization; every coalescing key (singleflight, result cache) includes that authorized scope so two callers with the same query text but different scope never share a scan or a cached result."
- KTD25: "Singleflight and the generation-keyed result cache key on the authorized scope, the complete normalized filter set, the embedding space, and the generation id together — never on (embedding_space, normalized_query_hash) alone." Plan risk note: this key shape is a correctness requirement, not a performance nicety.
- KTD1 (routes on the existing ck-mc module; subc transport 0.28-0.38 ms p50), KTD3 (dedicated compute pool; cancellation between scan blocks), KTD16 (the native ctx_search facade in crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs routes through the SAME engine; divergences documented per PARITY.md conventions only when mechanism, not behavior, differs).

## Key files
- crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs (route registration), new crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs, crates/mc-module/src/memory_tool.rs
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-transport.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search-backend.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts

## Approach
1. vector.search route: accepts query text or vector, filters, K, embedding-space identity, deadline; inference, normalization, scan, top-K stay daemon-side; cancellation checked between scan blocks.
2. Per KTD25: derive the caller's authorized project/session/trust scope server-side and intersect it with requested filters; coalescing keys include authorized scope + complete normalized filter set + embedding space + generation id.
3. Bounded interactive and background queues with reserved interactive capacity.
4. TS search-backend.ts seam: RustVectorBackend (route) and TsScanBackend (current scalar path) behind one interface; automatic fallback on connection failure/staleness per module-transport.ts conventions; a cold daemon serves the TS fallback while segments load, then flips.
5. Native ctx_search facade routes through the same engine (KTD16).

## Test scenarios
- Route round-trip on the hermetic daemon harness (packages/e2e-tests/src/rust-harness.ts, crates/mc-module/tests/real_daemon.rs): identical results TS-fallback vs Rust route on a seeded corpus.
- Two callers with the same query text but DIFFERENT authorized project scope never share a coalesced scan or a cached result (singleflight/cache-key fixture with deliberately colliding query hashes and differing scope).
- A request whose caller-supplied filter widens beyond the caller's authorized scope is served only the authorized subset, never the wider requested one.
- Deadline shorter than scan time: route returns cancelled; TS caller degrades per auto-search semantics (hint skipped, no error surfaced to user).
- Daemon down: backend seam falls back to TS scan with one loud log; results still returned.
- Two identical concurrent queries from the SAME authorized scope: one inference + one scan (singleflight counters).
- Background backfill saturating queues: an interactive query is still admitted within reserved capacity (latency assertion under load).
- Cold start: first search after daemon restart serves fallback; post-warm search serves the Rust path (state visible via status route).

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace + bun test + hermetic e2e group green.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (routes + authz + queues + fallback + facade) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: TsScanBackend reuses the existing scalar path behind the seam, no rewrite; perf: reserved interactive capacity asserted under load; ponytail-review: lean given R32/KTD25 key shape is load-bearing security, not a nicety; invariant-test-review: scope-isolation oracle uses deliberately colliding query hashes with differing scope - proves the R32 key shape, widened-filter test asserts served subset; test-strategy: hermetic e2e + counter-based singleflight oracles + adversarial fixtures

title: U14: Segment persistence + outbox consumer (push route)
description:
Phase 3. Crash-consistency tests are a hard gate for this unit (Verification Contract: crash suites for U14).

## Goal
Index generations survive restarts and stay fresh via the outbox — no full rebuild per insert — without the module opening context.db directly.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R14: "Vector index generations are immutable (base segment + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap), published atomically via a manifest; readers never observe a partial build, and old generations retire only after readers drain."
- R6 (transactional outbox maintenance), R31 (no new daemon; converge on existing machinery).
- KTD11: "Readers hold Arc<Mmap>-style generations; publish via manifest/ArcSwap; size-tiered compaction; per-segment local top-K merged at the end. Avoids full-generation rebuilds on every insert."
- KTD30: "U14's outbox consumer receives batches through a TS-initiated push route, not by the module opening context.db. The TS projection writer calls a vector.ingest route (established by U13) with pending outbox batches; the module writes segments and returns acknowledgment IDs; TS marks those outbox rows applied. crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs states the module never opens or attaches context.db, and that boundary changes only at U29's authority convergence — U14 does not anticipate it."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/segments.rs, src/manifest.rs (new)
- crates/mc-module/src/vector_search.rs; new vector.ingest route in crates/mc-module/src/lib.rs
- TS-side outbox drain in packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/retrieval-projection.ts

## Approach
1. Immutable base + bounded delta segments + tombstone bitmap; atomic manifest publish (fsync -> validate -> swap); readers pin generations; retire on drain; size-tiered compaction.
2. Per KTD30 (quoted above); acknowledgment is batched (no per-row transactions) on both sides.
3. Per-project/space byte-bounded residency with LRU eviction (replaces the process-global 256 MB decoded-pool behavior with an explicit budget).

## Test scenarios
- kill -9 between fsync and manifest swap: reopen serves the OLD generation intact (crash test with fault-injection points) — the R14 no-partial-reads oracle.
- Compaction removes tombstoned ordinals; post-compaction search equals pre-compaction search minus deletions (comparator).
- A reader holding an old generation during publish completes its scan on the old data; the next query sees the new generation.
- An outbox batch of N mutations pushed over vector.ingest lands in <= ceil(N/batch) transactions on the module side (statement counter), and applied_at marks EXACTLY ONCE on the TS side even under redelivery (idempotent ack test).
- The module process never issues a SQLite connection open against context.db during this unit's tests (process-level assertion) — the KTD30 boundary oracle.
- Eviction: exceeding the byte budget evicts the LRU project; the next query for it reloads from segments, correctness preserved.

## Verification
- cargo test; crash-consistency tests in CI; staleness SLA documented on the route (outbox consumed on search when pending, bounded added latency).
notes: reduce-complexity: segment machinery is R14-mandated; less-code: replaces the process-global 256MB decoded pool with one explicit budget; perf: batched acks kill per-row transactions (R29 direction); ponytail-review: no anticipation of U29 boundary change - module never opens context.db, held by process-level assertion; invariant-test-review: R14 no-partial-reads proven by kill-9 between fsync and manifest swap serving the OLD generation, exactly-once ack under redelivery; test-strategy: crash/fault-injection form + comparator + statement counters

title: U12: Kernel dispatch + top-K selection benchmarks
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Runtime-dispatched kernels and a measured top-K structure choice.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R28: measure, do not assume — variants land only on measured wins.
- KTD2: safe-SIMD-first with "runtime-dispatched NEON and AVX2/FMA variants (AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed) and no blanket target-cpu=native".

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/kernels.rs, src/topk.rs, benches/

## Approach
1. Kernel set: portable scalar, NEON (+dot-product extension where present), AVX2/FMA; feature-detected dispatch at index-open; no target-cpu=native artifacts.
2. Top-K candidates: fixed-capacity sorted array, binary heap, buffered select_nth_unstable — benched at K in {5, 32, 100}; the winner per K-band becomes the default. Losing structures do not ship as dead code (global Definition of Done: no dead experiment code).
3. Consecutive-window group max: retain max while walking (compartment_id, window_index) order instead of map+sort.

## Test scenarios
- All kernels agree with scalar EXACTLY (shared comparator harness from U10).
- Dispatch on a host lacking a feature falls back cleanly (force-disable flag in tests).
- Top-K structures agree with a full-sort reference across K values and duplicate scores.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench table (kernel x dims, structure x K) in the PR.
notes: reduce-complexity: ok; less-code: losing top-K structures REMOVED after measurement, only the winner ships (no dead experiment code); perf: measured K-band selection is the whole point; ponytail-review: AVX-512/VNNI only where deployed (KTD2), nothing speculative built; invariant-test-review: exact-agreement oracle vs scalar comparator including duplicate-score ties, force-disable fallback test; test-strategy: comparator property harness reused from U10 + bench table

title: U10: mc-vector crate: exact engine + trait
description:
Phase 3 — Rust dense engine. Develops in parallel with Phase 2 against synthetic corpora; integration comes in U13. Ships no ranking change itself, but its criterion baseline is the R28 correctness comparator that U15 measures against.

## Goal
The ID-first exact engine exists as a standalone crate with the VectorIndex abstraction.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R9: "Hot-path dense search runs in Rust over contiguous normalized vectors and returns compact (ordinal, score) pairs; stable IDs, text, and metadata hydrate only after fusion selects final candidates."
- R12: "Exact search is the default engine. ANN (HNSW) is added only behind the VectorIndex abstraction when measured thresholds are crossed: auto-search p95 above ~25 ms or active decoded index above ~128 MB for a scope." This unit lands the abstraction SEAM only — no HNSW work.
- R14: in-memory generation shape (immutable generation + tombstones).
- KTD1: "Dense engine lives in a new crates/mc-vector crate, exposed as routes on the existing ck-mc module ... mc-vector depends only on workspace-internal crates (no subc/cortexkit deps) so it builds and benches in isolation."
- KTD2: "Safe-SIMD-first kernels with runtime dispatch. The workspace is #![forbid(unsafe_code)] everywhere; mc-vector starts with a safe SIMD abstraction (pulp or wide) over a portable scalar baseline ... Unsafe is admitted only if benchmarks prove the safe abstraction leaves large wins on the table."
- KTD3: "Shard-local top-K per worker, merge workers x K; cancellation checked between scan blocks; never a shared heap in the scan loop."
- KTD10: "Row-major f32 exact scan is the baseline and correctness comparator."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/ (new: src/lib.rs, src/generation.rs, src/scan.rs, src/topk.rs, src/scratch.rs, criterion benches under benches/)
- root Cargo.toml workspace member

## Approach
1. Generation structure: packed normalized f32 row-major matrix, stable_ids: Vec<u64> (cold), filter bitmaps, tombstone bitset, group ranges (compartment -> ordinal range), generation id. QueryScratch with scores, seen-epoch, touched list, fixed-capacity top-K.
2. Dense u32 ordinals internally; (ordinal, score) output; stable-ID conversion only after top-K.
3. Normalize on index, normalize query once, dot product only; shard-local top-K, merge workers x K on a dedicated compute pool (KTD3).
4. VectorIndex trait: search(partition, query, k, filters, deadline), build_generation(docs), publish_generation(gen); ExactIndex is the first impl.
5. Scalar reference implementation kept as the correctness comparator; safe-SIMD kernels via pulp/wide (KTD2).
Directional: exact top-K with stable tie-breaking (score desc, ordinal asc).

## Test scenarios
- Property-test comparison: random corpus (1k x {128,384,1024}), random queries — SIMD scan top-K equals the scalar reference EXACTLY under stable tie-breaking, with and without tombstones.
- Deleted (tombstoned) ordinals never appear in results.
- K > live corpus returns all live, sorted.
- Deadline expiring mid-scan returns a cancelled error, NOT partial results presented as complete.
- Zero-vector and duplicate-vector inputs behave (no NaN; duplicates tie-break by ordinal).
- cargo bench baseline recorded for the scan across the U5 matrix dims.

## Verification
- cargo test --workspace; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; criterion baseline committed as a snapshot for U15 comparisons.
notes: reduce-complexity: VectorIndex trait seam is R12-mandated for future ANN, not speculative; less-code: scalar reference doubles as the correctness comparator - not dead code; perf: criterion baseline IS a deliverable (R28 comparator); ponytail-review: no HNSW, no unsafe - both trigger-gated per plan; invariant-test-review: SIMD-vs-scalar exact-equality property oracle under stable tie-breaking, deadline test asserts cancelled error rather than silent partials; test-strategy: property-based comparator + example edge cases (zero-vector, duplicates, K over corpus)

title: U11: Bitmap filters + adaptive scan
description:
Phase 3.

## Goal
Filters cut memory traffic, not just results.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R10: "Filtering (project, session, source type, trust, status, embedding space, time/ordinal range) uses bitmaps applied before or inside the scan so excluded vectors never touch the memory hierarchy; the scan strategy adapts to filter selectivity (dense masked scan, sparse gather, or segment skip)."

## Key files
- crates/mc-vector/src/filter.rs (new), src/scan.rs

## Approach
1. Bitmaps per project/session/source/trust/status/space + coarse ordinal/time ranges; raw bitsets for dense sets, Roaring-style containers for sparse; the crossover is MEASURED per architecture (bench, not assumed).
2. Strategy selection by allowed-set density: dense -> sequential masked scan; sparse -> set-bit enumeration + gather; range-restricted -> whole-segment skip via min/max metadata.

## Test scenarios
- Each strategy returns IDENTICAL results to the reference filter-then-scan for random filter sets at 0.1% / 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% selectivity.
- Segment-skip: a query restricted to an ordinal range touches only overlapping segments (assert via scan counters).
- Empty filter set returns empty WITHOUT touching vectors.
- Bench records bytes-touched per selectivity point — proves the R10 mechanism (excluded vectors are not read), not just output correctness.

## Verification
- cargo test; bench comparison in PR notes.
notes: reduce-complexity: three strategies are R10-mandated adaptivity; less-code: minimal; perf: bytes-touched counter proves the mechanism (excluded vectors never read), not just outputs; ponytail-review: raw-vs-Roaring crossover measured per architecture, not assumed - already gated; invariant-test-review: strategy-equivalence property vs reference filter-then-scan across selectivities + counter-based traffic oracle; test-strategy: property comparison + mechanism counters

title: U9: Reader re-pointing to claims
description:
Phase 2. Completes KTD4's coexistence exit.

## Goal
Search, mural, dreamer, and module state-sync read claim current-state through one API; the legacy write path retires.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R1 (immutable revisions).
- R8: the retirement step is a fence-bumped migration and follows the rollout order — ship all binaries with new version support first, then migrate.
- KTD4 (exit): "readers re-point incrementally (U9); ... the legacy write path retires in a later fence-bumped migration."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/search.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/mural/resolve-mural.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/dreamer/ (classify, map-memories, verify-gate, task-executor)
- packages/plugin/src/hooks/magic-context/module-state-sync.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory.ts

## Approach
1. Introduce a claims read API (current revision + state + trust) and move each reader over ONE AT A TIME; the module wire (state-sync, mirror) keeps its existing memories-shaped payload fed from the projection until U29 upgrades the protocol. Dashboards/TUI (/ctx-status memory counts) keep working through the compatibility projection until re-pointed.
2. Once all readers are re-pointed, a follow-up migration demotes memories to a pure derived projection (writes forbidden by trigger except the projection writer) — the fence-bumped retirement step in the R8 rollout order.

## Test scenarios
- Each re-pointed reader has a parity test: same fixture DB, IDENTICAL output before/after re-pointing (mural render, dreamer classification input set, state-sync page bytes).
- Search results identical on a fixture corpus pre/post re-point (ranking fixture).
- Post-retirement: direct memories write from an unprivileged path raises; the projection-writer path succeeds.

## Verification
- Full bun test + packages/e2e-tests memory/dreamer scenarios green.
notes: reduce-complexity: one-reader-at-a-time is the simple shape; less-code: retirement migration DELETES the legacy write path - net negative diff; perf: no hot-path change, parity-guarded; ponytail-review: ctx-status readers ride the projection until re-pointed, no extra shim; invariant-test-review: parity oracles are byte/set-identical golden fixtures per reader + negative write-fence trigger test; test-strategy: golden parity examples + negative write test

title: U8: Retrieval projection, outbox, generations, embedding spaces
description:
Phase 2.

## Goal
The rebuildable search projection and its maintenance plumbing exist; embeddings become content-addressed and space-keyed.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R3: "Every search structure (FTS tables, vector matrices, retrieval documents) is a derived projection, rebuildable from authoritative tables; corruption or loss of a derived index never damages or disables authoritative memory."
- R4: "An embedding space is a full contract — provider, model revision, tokenizer revision, query/passage templates, pooling, normalization, dimensions, metric, max input tokens, chunking version, text-view version — not a model name."
- R5: "Vectors are content-addressed: one physical vector per (embedding space, text-view version, content hash); documents reference vectors through postings, and exact duplicates are scored once."
- R6: "Index maintenance flows through a transactional outbox plus per-scope generation counters; cache and index validity checks are single indexed point lookups, never COUNT(*)/MAX(id) corpus probes or wall-clock TTLs."
- KTD9: "A search_index_generation(scope_id, embedding_space_id, generation, row_count, checksum) row increments transactionally with every mutation; cache validation is one indexed point lookup. Two explicit modes: exact mode always scans the packed index; lexical-gated mode fetches vectors only for lexical candidate IDs — never decode a full pool to score a candidate subset. ... a generation is scoped to that full identity, so changing any one field opens a new space and a new generation rather than silently reusing vectors."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- new packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/retrieval-projection.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory-embeddings.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/project-embedding-registry.ts
- tests co-located (also touches embedding-cache.ts and compartment-chunk-embedding.ts staleness probes)

## Approach
1. retrieval_documents (entity_type/entity_id/revision_id, view_kind, title, identifiers, body, content_hash, trust_state, authority_rank, validity window); index_outbox (document, space, operation, applied_at); search_index_generation per KTD9; embedding_spaces normalizing what embedding_registrations holds PLUS every R4 identity field — ALL ELEVEN fields participate in the space's unique identity, not just the six embedding_registrations already tracks.
2. document_embeddings keyed (embedding_space_id, text_view_version, content_hash) with a postings table document<->vector (R5); migrate existing memory_embeddings / compartment_chunk_embeddings / git_commit_embeddings content into the new shape via REBUILD (they are derived; no data-loss concern), keeping old tables until U9 re-points readers.
3. Projection writer subscribes to claim/tool-event mutations through the outbox INSIDE the same transaction; a rebuild command regenerates the whole projection from authoritative tables (the R3 proof).
4. Replace the 60 s embedding cache TTL and the COUNT(*)/MAX(id) staleness probes with generation point-lookups (embedding-cache.ts, compartment-chunk-embedding.ts); implement exact vs lexical-gated fetch modes (KTD9).

## Test scenarios
- Claim revision insert produces exactly one outbox row and one generation bump in the SAME transaction (rollback removes both).
- Two documents with identical content hash in one space share one physical vector; postings expand both at retrieval.
- Rebuild-from-scratch on a corrupted projection reproduces IDENTICAL document set and content hashes (R3 rebuildability oracle).
- Generation check: mutation invalidates the cached pool via one point lookup; unchanged generation serves the cached pool with ZERO corpus probes (statement counter).
- Lexical-gated mode fetches only candidate vectors (assert decoded byte count << full pool).
- Pending-embedding documents are lexically searchable immediately (outbox row present, vector absent).
- Changing any ONE of the eleven embedding_spaces identity fields (e.g., chunking version or max input tokens) on an otherwise-identical registration produces a distinct space id and a fresh generation; vectors from the old space are never scored against the new space's query.

## Verification
- bun test; migration tests; a projection-rebuild e2e script run documented in the unit's PR.
notes: reduce-complexity: unit is OVERSIZED (projection + outbox + generations + spaces) - noted per conversion constraints, not split; less-code: old embedding tables kept only until U9 re-points readers, removal scheduled there; perf: generation point-lookups replace COUNT(*)/TTL corpus probes - hot-path win; ponytail-review: all eleven R4 identity fields now prevents silent vector reuse later, plan-mandated; invariant-test-review: R3 proven by rebuild-equality oracle, R6 by same-transaction rollback oracle, KTD9 modes by statement/decoded-byte counters; test-strategy: example + counter-based mechanism oracles

title: U7: Memories-to-claims backfill + dual-read
description:
Phase 2. The crash-injection suite for the write triple is a hard gate for this unit.

## Goal
Every existing memory row becomes a claim + revision; memories continues to serve unported readers as a maintained projection.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- KD3 / R8: "Existing memory rows migrate forward into claims; derived indexes rebuild from scratch" — two truth models forever is worse than one bounded migration.
- R1: immutable revisions.
- KTD4: "Claims migration is additive with dual-read ... memories becomes a maintained compatibility projection so search, mural, dreamer, module state-sync, and the mc-store mirror keep working unmodified; readers re-point incrementally (U9); duplicates collapse by normalized hash during coexistence; the legacy write path retires in a later fence-bumped migration."
- KTD21 (atomicity invariant): "U7's backfill runs in the migration transaction for corpora under the U5-measured scale threshold; above it, the lazy startup backfill (v22 pattern) applies, gated by schema_migrations_meta, with reads served from the memories projection until the backfill's completion checkpoint flips. The claim revision write, the memories projection update, and their outbox/generation side effects commit atomically in one transaction (in either backfill mode) — a crash between them must never leave the two reader surfaces disagreeing."

## Key files
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/migrations.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-memory.ts
- packages/plugin/src/features/magic-context/memory/storage-claims.ts
- migration test

## Approach
1. Backfill migration: each active/archived memory row -> claim (subject/scope from project + category + normalized_hash) + revision 1 (content, category); merged_from JSON arrays -> claim_evidence/merge lineage rows; supersession -> conflict/supersede relations; verification rows -> verification_events.
2. Protocol per KTD21 (quoted above). The scale-threshold value is set from U5's scale measurements, not guessed here.
3. Writes go claims-first: storage-memory.ts mutators create a revision and update the memories projection row in the SAME transaction as the outbox/generation bump — this triple never partially commits. Dedup by normalized hash prevents double-surfacing during coexistence.
Execution note: write characterization tests over storage-memory.ts mutators BEFORE rewiring them — this is legacy-shaped code with many consumers.

## Test scenarios
- Backfill of a seeded v78 DB (memories with counters, supersession, merges, verifications) produces claims whose revision-1 content hashes equal the source rows; row counts reconcile.
- Post-migration memory update creates revision 2 and updates the projection row; both reads (claims API, legacy getMemoriesByProject) agree.
- Dedup: identical normalized hash surfaces once in search during coexistence.
- Mural, dreamer classify, and state-sync smoke: existing co-located tests keep passing UNMODIFIED (projection compatibility).
- Crash simulation: interrupted lazy backfill (if that path is used) resumes idempotently.
- Crash injection at EVERY point inside the claims-first write triple (revision insert, projection update, outbox/generation bump): after recovery, the claims read and the legacy getMemoriesByProject read ALWAYS agree — neither observes a partial write (KTD21 atomicity oracle).

## Verification
- Full bun test for packages/plugin; packages/e2e-tests memory scenarios green; crash-injection suite for the write triple green.
notes: reduce-complexity: dual-mode backfill is KTD21-mandated, not accidental; less-code: characterization tests first prevent rework on legacy mutators with many consumers; perf: lazy backfill path keeps startup bounded above the scale threshold; ponytail-review: threshold value comes from U5 measurement, not invented here; invariant-test-review: KTD21 atomicity proven by agreement of BOTH reader surfaces after crash injection at EVERY seam of the write triple - proves the invariant, not just execution; test-strategy: fault-injection form chosen for the write triple, characterization + example tests for mutators

title: U6: Claims/evidence authoritative schema
description:
Phase 2 — Domain model and retrieval projection.

## Goal
The immutable domain model exists: projects, episodes, source spans, observations, claims, claim revisions, evidence links, conflicts, verification events.

## Governing constraints (quoted)
- R1: "A change to claim content creates a new immutable claim revision; indexed text is never mutated in place."
- R2: "Every claim revision links to its evidence: observations extracted from source spans, with extractor provenance and an independence key."
- R8: "Schema changes are forward-only and additive, honor the schema-version fence and the multi-process migration-on-open guard, and follow a documented binary rollout order; all pre-existing memory rows migrate forward into claims." Rollout order: ship ALL binaries (OpenCode plugin, Pi plugin, CLI, ck-mc) with new version support FIRST, then let the migration run.

## Key files

title: F16 fence read-loop emissions before connection Goodbye
description: Finding: Shutdown queues connection Goodbye without a producer barrier for read-loop control/rejection emissions. Severity CONSIDER (P2), concurrency correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/runtime.rs, connection.rs, dispatch.rs/wire.rs and lifecycle tests. Shutdown freezes route admission and drains routes, but read loops can still start/finish catalog or server_busy terminals while shutdown queues Goodbye, allowing a terminal after Goodbye. Introduce a generation/read-loop emission fence or explicit producer join so every started control/rejection send completes before Goodbye and no later send begins. Extend the existing shutdown terminal-order test with deterministic barriers, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: All control/rejection emissions started before shutdown are queued before connection Goodbye; no read-loop emission can begin afterward; deterministic tests cover catalog and rejection races; generation teardown remains bounded; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F15 bound outbound admission with one deadline
description: Finding: Outbound byte-budget and writer-queue waits are unbounded. Severity CONSIDER (P2), reliability. Files: crates/mc-host/src/dispatch.rs, wire.rs/config.rs and dispatch/wire/lifecycle tests. emit_frame waits separately for egress ByteBudget and writer queue with only generation cancellation; a live slow consumer can retain request/settlement resources indefinitely. Apply one absolute operation deadline across both admission waits, using existing timing policy where possible, and retire the generation on expiry. Extend existing stalled-writer/byte-budget tests with paused-time or deterministic barriers, confirm failure, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Every outbound operation has one absolute deadline spanning byte charge and writer queue admission; deadline expiry retires generation and releases all charges/resources; deterministic tests cover both stages and prove the second receives only remaining budget; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F11 reserve or cache catalog response before serialization
description: Finding: Catalog response memory is allocated before resident-byte reservation. Severity CONSIDER (P2), performance/correctness. Files: crates/mc-host/src/control.rs, runtime.rs, connection.rs and catalog tests. Every catalog.list builds a fresh serde_json Value/Vec before emit_frame charges output, so concurrent connections can allocate copies outside max_resident_bytes. Prefer serializing and validating immutable catalog variants once at startup, or reserve an exact conservative bound before serialization and transfer that charge. Extend existing catalog/control tests with deterministic allocation/reuse/accounting coverage, confirm the old behavior fails the new contract, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog serialization is cached at startup or fully reserved before allocation; repeated/concurrent catalog.list calls do not create uncharged full catalog copies; filters remain truthful and frame bounded; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified catalog response caching, one-deadline outbound admission, and read-producer fencing before Goodbye; focused and full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/strict lib-test clippy pass.

title: F10 enforce publication permissions independent of umask
description: Finding: Umask can strip required owner permissions. Severity CONSIDER (P2), correctness/security. Files: crates/mc-host/src/instance.rs and tests/instance_security.rs. Directory/file creation modes are masked by umask, so a restrictive umask may yield unreadable publication credentials even though creation through the fd succeeds. Explicitly fchmod every newly created private directory component to 0700 and publication/secret files to 0600 before publication, while retaining symlink/race defenses. Extend existing instance security coverage with a subprocess or serialized umask test, confirm it fails before the fix, implement minimally, and run focused/full mc-host tests plus fmt/check/clippy.
acceptance_criteria: New private directories are exactly owner rwx and credential/publication files exactly owner rw regardless of restrictive umask; no process-global umask test races; existing nofollow/identity cleanup defenses remain intact; mc-host fmt/check/clippy/tests pass.
close_reason: Resolved with explicit 0700/0600 fchmod behavior independent of umask. Added a subprocess test under umask 0777, confirmed the pre-fix open_component failure, then verified publication remains readable with exact owner modes. Instance unit/security tests pass.
